textual.observation: A walkthrough describes selling 15 OneCoin for a stated return of €35.14, entering a transaction password, placing an order, and receiving coins in a Cash account today or tomorrow.

evidence.quote: for example € and so by selling 15 coins I will receive 35,14 €.
And in this field I put the transaction password.
Your order has successfully been ready It means that we have sold our coins in the external exchange and today or tomorrow you will receive your coins to the Cash account

textual.context: The speaker presents this as a first-person walkthrough or demonstration; whether viewers are being asked to perform the same steps is unclear.
textual.potential_relevance: The stated monetary return and near-term account receipt are linked to an exchange order and entry of a transaction password, creating a specific transaction-and-credential relationship for later context assessment.
textual.limitations: The records do not independently establish that the order executed, that the stated amount was paid, or that any coins reached the account.

visual.observation: A OneCoin exchange "Sell" form shows a market order for 15 coins at a displayed sell price of 2.343, a transaction value of 35.14 EUR, a stated Onecoin transaction fee of 0.38 Onecoins, an expiry date, a "Transaction password" field, and a "PLACE ORDER" button.
visual.context: Interactive exchange/order-entry interface; the sampled frames show data entry and focus on the password field, but not a confirmed submission.
visual.potential_relevance: The interface links a requested authorization/password entry and order-placement action to a specified asset sale, fee, and expiry condition; this relationship could merit review as a financial-transfer mechanism without establishing deception or loss.
visual.limitations: These frames do not establish who controls the account, whether the password was accepted, whether the order was submitted or executed, or whether any funds or assets changed hands.

textual_context_notes.observation: The exchange is described differently across the records: internal in the description and external in the ASR.

evidence.quote: sell OneCoin in our internal exchange.
we have sold our coins in the external exchange

visual_context_notes.observation: The visible interface is branded OneCoin and presents dashboard, exchange, mining, account, and member-related sections.
A later exchange view visibly shows transaction-history entries and buy/sell price panels, but the sampled chronology does not establish that the earlier sell form caused any displayed transaction.

annotation.contextual_rationale: This video is scam content because it presents OneCoin as a tradable asset and demonstrates an internal sell order, claiming that 15 coins will produce 35.14 euros and a near-term Cash account credit. A separately cited U.S. Justice Department account establishes that OneCoin was marketed and sold as a fraudulent cryptocurrency and that its claimed value was internally set. The tutorial's transaction-password field is ordinary account verification, not a request to disclose credentials to the presenter; the video does not prove that the claimed cash-out occurred.
annotation.fine_grained_rationale: S05 describes the OneCoin token-value proposition illustrated by the claimed conversion of coins into cash in this tutorial. The separately cited Justice Department source establishes the program's fraudulent token sales and internally set value. The video does not show a new viewer buying tokens or receiving the claimed cash; the program-level basis is external. Entering a password into one's own sell-order form does not qualify as an account-access or sensitive-data cue credential solicitation.
